message.content: unexplained magic number 0.05. is this a new fee? add a named const + a test or revert.
good. error includes status: throw new Error(`user fetch failed: ${r.status}`).
returns row array. caller probably expects User|null. either: change to .then(rows => rows[0] ?? null), or rename method to getUsers.
good test, asserts shape not just truthy. add a paired failing-case test: invalid creds throws or returns null.
don't log payment amounts to stdout — pii/pci concern. either redact (amount > 0 ? '<amount>' : '0') or remove.
revert. the filter/map version was clearer + faster. unless this is hot-path and you measured, don't undo functional style.
silent drop hides quota errors from caller. either: surface via callback, or log via your error tracker. comment promises silence but caller has no way to know save failed.
TODOs without owner+date rot. either: assign + date it, or open a ticket and reference the ticket id. "when we have time" = never.
no check on PUT response. silently swallows S3 failures. wrap with `if (!resp.ok) throw` after fetch.
leaks full user object including any hash/email fields not meant for client. shape it: `res.json({ id: user.id, name: user.name })` or define a public-user serializer.
clean. one small note: typeof t === 'undefined' on first call passes fine to clearTimeout, but consider adding explicit cancel method so caller can clear pending fire on unmount.
good. but the previous commit still has the live key in git history — rotate the key NOW, don't just delete the line. also add STRIPE_KEY to .env.example with a placeholder.
hardcoded codes don't scale. move to a discount-codes config (map: code → multiplier). lets ops add codes without a deploy.

good. test isolates state via beforeEach. consider also: cart.reload() in test vs production — is it the same path, or does the test bypass code? if bypass, test passes but real reload could still fail.
both sentry + console is fine in dev. but in prod console.error is noise sentry already captured. wrap: if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') console.error(err).
